symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1474 "auto created module role is potential security issue": a new microflow, nanoflow or page in a module with no module roles created `<Module>.User` ("Auto-created default role for mxcli document access") and granted the document to it — a security role nobody asked for, open to every user role later mapped to it, and only narrowable by an explicit revoke.
cause: defaultDocumentAccessRoles (cmd_security_defaults.go) created the role to keep `mx check` green, and three passes mirrored it: the exec note (reportAutoRoleGrant), check's grant resolver (recordAutoDocumentRole) and MDL-SEC21's simulation (flowAccessSim.defaultRoles). Removed: a new document now starts with no allowed roles in every module; MOVE remaps to same-named target roles and never creates one.
insight: A default that writes security is not a convenience: the earlier fix (an exec note saying the grant happened) made it visible but kept it, and the issue was about the role existing at all. Removing an implicit default means enumerating every pass that SIMULATES it — exec, check --references and MDL-SEC21 each had their own copy, and a missed one makes check accept a grant exec refuses; TestCheckGrantReferences_AgreesWithExec on PedApp is the test that catches that drift. Scripts that granted to <Module>.User without creating it (doctype-tests/02b, ledger-54/67) now need `create module role`; MDL-SEC21 already names that fix for a flow used from a page. The description marker stays recognised: projects from older mxcli still hold the role, and `create module role M.User` must keep adopting it.
